title: The Charge for Extra Days on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## The quantity to be arrived at

The charge for keeping hire kit longer than the agreement was written for rests on the extra days asked for and the daily figure those days are charged at.

**The extra days.** The extra days are the calendar days from the date written on the agreement to the date the guest has asked the kit to be kept to, and they are never more than the package's extension limit and never below zero. The limit is the one held against the package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line the agreement is written on.

**Days given free.** No day of the extension is given free. The days given free are taken off the extra days before the charge is worked out, and the extra days are never taken below zero after they are taken off.

**The daily figure and the fee.** Each extra day is charged at the package's multi-day day rate, and the package's extension fee is raised on top of the extra days.

**Where the guest is staying.** The daily figure is taken in full, without where the guest is staying weighed against it.

**The notice given.** The daily figure is taken in full, without the notice the guest gave weighed against it.

**A helmet.** Nothing is added to the daily figure for a helmet carried on into the extra days.

**The fee.** The package's extension fee is raised in full on top.

**How the parts meet.** The daily figure is first taken at the resident share, and the figure that step leaves is then taken at the notice share, so the notice share acts on what the resident share left and not on the daily figure the step before it started from; the helmet addition is added to the figure the two shares leave, and the extension fee is added once to the whole rather than to each day. The charge is worked out once and rounded half up to two decimal places.

An extension is recorded before the kit falls due, and kit already overdue is handled as a late hand-in instead. Where the package is one the collective does not extend, no charge for extra days arises under this rule and the agreement runs to the date written on it. A season lease is not extended at all.

## The working on a hypothetical extension

Take an agreement on a package whose multi-day day rate is 39.00 USD, whose extension fee is 10.00 USD and whose extension limit is 7 days, written to the 14th of January, on which the guest has asked for the kit to be kept to the 17th.

| Step | Working | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the extra days asked for | the 14th to the 17th of January, within the limit of 7 days | 3 days |
| days given free | none | 3 days |
| the daily figure | the package's multi-day day rate | 39.00 USD |
| the resident share | the daily figure taken in full | 39.00 USD |
| the notice share | the 39.00 USD that step left, taken in full | 39.00 USD |
| a helmet carried on | nothing added to the 39.00 USD the two shares left | 39.00 USD |
| the days at the daily figure | 3 days at 39.00 USD | 117.00 USD |
| the extension fee | 10.00 USD added once to the whole | 127.00 USD |
| the charge | worked out once and rounded half up to two decimal places | 127.00 USD |

Had the guest asked for the kit to be kept 10 days beyond the date written on the agreement, the extra days would stand at 7, the package's limit.

## Points of judgement

**The second share starts from what the first left.** The notice share is measured against the figure the resident share leaves, not against the daily figure that share started from, and the helmet addition joins the figure the two shares leave rather than the figure they started from.

**One working, one rounding.** The charge is arrived at by a single working, and the rounding half up to two decimal places falls at the end of that working.

**The fee is added once.** The package's extension fee is added to the whole, not to each extra day.

**A package the collective does not extend.** No charge for extra days arises under this rule, and the agreement runs to the date written on it.
